en.bdb: Example of double-talker and the double-faced mirror,

verses.gurmukhi: ਦੇਖਿ ਦੁਭਿਤੀ ਆਰਸੀ ਮਜਲਸ ਹਥੋ ਹਥੀ ਨਚੈ।
verses.translit_en: dhekh dhubhitee aarasee majalas hatho hathee nachai|

en.bdb: Double-faced i.e. uneven minor moves hand to hand in the assembly (because nobody likes it).

verses.gurmukhi: ਦੁਖੋ ਦੁਖੁ ਦੁਬਾਜਰੀ ਘਰਿ ਘਰਿ ਫਿਰੈ ਪਰਾਈ ਖਚੈ।
verses.translit_en: dhukho dhukh dhubaajaree ghar ghar firai paraiee khachai|

en.bdb: Similarly a double-talker like a prostitute engrossed in other's homes moves from door to door.

verses.gurmukhi: ਅਗੋ ਹੋਇ ਸੁਹਾਵਣੀ ਮੁਹਿ ਡਿਠੈ ਮਾਣਸ ਚਹਮਚੈ।
verses.translit_en: ago hoi suhaavanee muh ddiThai maanas chahamachai|

en.bdb: At first she looks pretty and men are pleased to see her face

verses.gurmukhi: ਪਿਛਹੁ ਦੇਖਿ ਡਰਾਵਣੀ ਇਕੋ ਮੁਹੁ ਦੁਹੁ ਜਿਨਸਿ ਵਿਰਚੈ।
verses.translit_en: pichhahu dhekh ddaraavanee iko muh dhuh jinas virachai|

en.bdb: But later she is found to be dreadful because her single face possesses two images.

verses.gurmukhi: ਖੇਹਿ ਪਾਇ ਮੁਹੁ ਮਾਂਜੀਐ ਫਿਰਿ ਫਿਰਿ ਮੈਲੁ ਭਰੈ ਰੰਗਿ ਕਚੈ।
verses.translit_en: kheh pai muh maa(n)jeeaai fir fir mail bharai ra(n)g kachai|

en.bdb: Even cleaned with ashes, such double-faced mirror becomes filthy again.

verses.gurmukhi: ਧਰਮਰਾਇ ਜਮੁ ਇਕੁ ਹੈ ਧਰਮੁ ਅਧਰਮੁ ਨ ਭਰਮ ਪਰਚੈ।
verses.translit_en: dharamarai jam ik hai dharam adharam na bharam parachai|

en.bdb: Yama, the Lord of dharma is one; he accepts dharma but does not get pleased by the delusions of wickedness.
Truthful gurmukhs ultimately attain the truth.
